name: The Mountain Goats
label: Merge
lede: John Darnielle started out taping songs into a Panasonic boombox while working a psych-ward job in Southern California. Thirty-odd years on, the Mountain Goats are a four-piece playing rooms where the crowd sings back songs about wrestlers, goths, Dungeons & Dragons and his stepfather.

eras.title: Songs into a boombox in Claremont
eras.text: John Darnielle worked on a psychiatric ward and taped songs straight into a cassette boombox. The Mountain Goats were whatever he recorded that week, out on cassettes and 7-inches from tiny labels like Shrimper.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Mountain Goats · Wikipedia: John Darnielle
years.h: Shrimper puts out the first Mountain Goats tape
years.p: Dennis Callaci's label releases Taboo VI: The Homecoming, John Darnielle's first recording as the Mountain Goats. The band name comes from Screamin' Jay Hawkins's song Yellow Coat.
years.xp: Darnielle was born in 1967. He was working on the psychiatric ward at Metropolitan State Hospital in Norwalk, California, while studying Classics and English at Pitzer College, where he double-majored and graduated in 1995.

years.h: Zopilote Machine brings in the Bright Mountain Choir
years.p: The first full Mountain Goats album, on Ajax, and the only one with the whole choir, an all-girl reggae group. Its bassist, [[Rachel Ware|a3c4ff1f-ab55-4cd9-b914-ab69fa2b7ab8]], plays live with John Darnielle until 1995.
years.xp: Ware kept playing bass in the studio until 1996 and left after the sessions for Nothing for Juice.

years.h: Darnielle vows to clean the swearing out of his songs
years.p: Announced in November 1996: no more profanity in Mountain Goats songs, in the hope that listeners take in what the songs are saying.

eras.title: A wedding, a long quiet, then a real studio
eras.text: Darnielle married in Iowa and the releases thinned out. In 2002 he made the boombox album that closed the boombox era, and the same year went into a studio with a full band for 4AD.

years.h: Darnielle marries Lalitree Chavanothai in Colo, Iowa
years.p: The wedding is in April. Mountain Goats output slows for the next few years.

years.h: All Hail West Texas arrives, recorded entirely on the boombox
years.p: Emperor Jones releases the album John Darnielle taped in 2001 on his Panasonic RX-FT500. The cover promises fourteen songs about seven people, two houses, a motorcycle and a locked treatment facility for adolescent boys.
years.xp:
The Best Ever Death Metal Band in Denton opens it, and Jenny introduces a character who comes back 21 years later on Jenny from Thebes. Darnielle has called it the culmination of his lo-fi style. It was the last Mountain Goats album recorded entirely on the boombox until 2020.

He had fifteen outtakes he meant to give away free one day. After hearing about the leak of Hail and Farewell, Gothenburg, he destroyed them. Pitchfork scored the album 8.2.

years.h: Tallahassee puts a failing marriage in a Florida house and a band in a studio
years.p: The first Mountain Goats album made with a full band in a studio, for 4AD. It follows the Alpha couple.
years.xp: No Children, the couple's poisonous duet with themselves, kept finding new audiences for two decades and had a second life on TikTok in the 2020s.

years.h: Peter Hughes, touring bassist since Ware, goes full-time
years.p: [[Peter Hughes|012931a2-fa02-425b-8f23-908f73eb7b85]], who had played bass on tours after Rachel Ware left, becomes a full member in 2002.

eras.title: Telling on himself
eras.text: Darnielle moved to Durham, North Carolina and stopped hiding behind characters. With producer John Vanderslice he made one record about his speed years and one about the stepfather who beat him, while a band grew up around him: Hughes, then Jon Wurster of Superchunk.

years.h: Darnielle moves to Durham, North Carolina
years.p: Durham is a short drive from Chapel Hill, where Merge is based, and becomes the band's base.

years.h: We Shall All Be Healed goes autobiographical, with Vanderslice at the board
years.p: John Darnielle's first openly autobiographical Mountain Goats album, and the first with producer John Vanderslice, is about friends addicted to methamphetamine in Portland, moved to Pomona, California.

years.cap: John Darnielle and Peter Hughes on stage, February 2005
years.src: Wikipedia: The Mountain Goats · Wikipedia: John Darnielle
years.h: The Sunset Tree takes on the stepfather
years.p: John Darnielle's 4AD album about growing up in Claremont with a stepfather who abused him. Its song This Year becomes a live staple.
years.xp: Produced by John Vanderslice, and dedicated to the stepfather it describes. The same stepfather took young Darnielle to pro wrestling at the Grand Olympic Auditorium in Los Angeles, which is where Beat the Champ comes from ten years later.

years.cap: The Mountain Goats at the Northstar Bar, September 2007
years.h: Superchunk's drummer sits in for a tour and doesn't leave
years.p: [[Jon Wurster|feab5f8f-f5ac-4e63-92a8-466dde483f8c]] plays the last leg of the Get Lonely tour in 2007 and is still behind the kit.

years.h: Franklin Bruno and Annie Clark both play on Heretic Pride
years.p: Clark records as [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]]. She and [[Franklin Bruno|e215dcc5-4193-493c-ac7a-436625bcf4e9]] appear alongside John Darnielle, Peter Hughes and Jon Wurster.

years.h: Darnielle's 33⅓ book on Black Sabbath turns out to be a novel
years.p: Master of Reality follows a young man held in a psychiatric facility who is trying to get back his confiscated Walkman and the tape of the album. It is not music criticism.

years.h: Moon Colony Bloodbath imagines organ harvesting on the Moon
years.p: A limited vinyl EP, conceived as a concept record about organ-harvesting colonies.

years.h: Stephen Colbert, a self-declared fan, gives the band its first TV spot
years.p: The Mountain Goats play Psalms 40:2 from The Life of the World to Come on The Colbert Report, October 6, 2009.
years.xp: The Life of the World to Come, out that month on 4AD, has twelve songs each named for a Bible verse. Ten years later, in July 2019, Colbert sang This Year with the band on The Late Show.

eras.title: Down the road to Merge
eras.text: Signing with Merge put the band in its own backyard. The records got more specific, a wrestling album, an album with no guitar, a Dungeons & Dragons album, while Darnielle turned into a novelist on the side.

years.h: The Mountain Goats sign to Merge after eight years at 4AD
years.p: Chapel Hill's Merge Records is also home to Superchunk, the other band of drummer Jon Wurster.

years.h: All Eternals Deck opens the Merge years
years.p: Merge releases every Mountain Goats album from this one, out in March 2011, through Jenny from Thebes in 2023.

years.h: Matthew E. White arranges the horns on Transcendental Youth
years.p: The Mountain Goats add a horn section for the October 2012 album. The clip is their Newport Folk Festival set from the same year.

years.h: Merge puts All Hail West Texas on vinyl for the first time
years.p: The July 23 reissue adds seven unreleased songs and an 1,800-word essay by John Darnielle. Pitchfork names it Best New Reissue.
years.xp: Pitchfork had scored the original 8.2. The reissue gets 9.0.

years.h: A novel about a mail-order role-playing game makes the National Book Award list
years.p: Wolf in White Van, John Darnielle's first novel, follows a disfigured man who runs the game. It comes out September 16, 2014.
years.xp: The nomination for the National Book Award for Fiction arrives two days after publication.

years.h: Beat the Champ goes to the wrestling ring
years.p: The Mountain Goats sing about the pro wrestlers John Darnielle watched as a kid. Multi-instrumentalist Matt Douglas plays on it and becomes a full member.

years.h: Rian Johnson gets a Last Jedi song out of Darnielle
years.p: Darnielle records a joke song for the director, with a title about a Jedi who eats the other Jedi's bones.

years.h: Goths leaves the guitar off entirely
years.p: John Darnielle writes about the goths he grew up around, fans of the Cure, Bauhaus and Joy Division, and the KROQ playlists that fed them.
play: Andrew Eldritch Is Moving Back to Leeds

years.h: A podcast goes through All Hail West Texas song by song
years.p: I Only Listen to the Mountain Goats comes from John Darnielle and Welcome to Night Vale co-creator Joseph Fink.

years.h: In League with Dragons turns Dungeons & Dragons into an album
years.p: Announced in January 2019 with the single Younger, and out April 26.

eras.title: The boombox comes out again
eras.text: When the pandemic shut everything down, Darnielle dug the old Panasonic out and made a tape album. Four more records followed in four years, then Peter Hughes, the bassist since 2002, stepped away.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Mountain Goats · Wikipedia: All Hail West Texas
years.h: Lockdown sends Darnielle back to the Panasonic for Songs for Pierre Chuvin
years.p: He records ten songs straight into the RX-FT500, the first time since All Hail West Texas. The themes come from Pierre Chuvin's book A Chronicle of the Last Pagans.

years.h: Getting Into Knives is cut at Sam Phillips Recording, just ahead of lockdown
years.p: It is the full-band counterpart to the boombox tape the Mountain Goats put out that spring.

years.h: Dark in Here is cut at FAME in Muscle Shoals
years.p: The next full-band album, eight months after Getting Into Knives, recorded in Alabama.

years.h: A true-crime novel from Darnielle, Devil House, earns an Edgar nomination
years.p: John Darnielle's third novel, about a true-crime writer, is published January 25, 2022.
years.xp: It is nominated for the Edgar Award for Best Novel the following year.

years.h: Bleed Out comes out of a pandemic's worth of action movies
years.p: John Darnielle builds the songs around the action films he watched in early lockdown. One of them is called Training Montage.

years.h: Jenny, from a 2002 song, gets a whole rock opera
years.p: The Mountain Goats build Jenny from Thebes around the woman first sung about on All Hail West Texas 21 years earlier.

years.h: Bassist Peter Hughes, with the band since 2002, announces he's leaving
years.p: Hughes announces in August 2024 that he's stepping away after nearly 30 years in and around the band, citing his health and sanity among other reasons.

eras.title: Off Merge, onto their own
eras.text: After fifteen years on Merge, and with a new bassist, the band started putting records out through its own label, Cadmean Dawn. Darnielle kept writing at the same absurd pace.

years.h: Cameron Ralston takes over on bass
years.p: The lineup is now John Darnielle, Jon Wurster, Matt Douglas and Ralston.

years.h: Through This Fire Across from Peter Balkan starts as a dream
years.p: John Darnielle writes the dream down. The album, out November 7, 2025, is the first after 15 years with Merge, released on Cadmean Dawn.

years.h: Nine months later, Days
years.p: The Mountain Goats release it August 7, 2026 on Cadmean Dawn.
